statement.p: Suppose \vec{F}(x,y) = (3 x - 3 y) \vec{i} + 2 x \vec{j} and C is the counter-clockwise oriented sector of a circle centered at the origin with radius 3 and central angle \pi / 3. Use Green's theorem to calculate the circulation of \vec{F} around C.

solution.p: Let D be the region enclosed by the curve C.

First note that the curve has a positive orientation. We will use Green's Theorem. We have P = 3 x - 3 y, \; Q = 2 x, therefore \frac{\partial Q}{\partial x} - \frac{\partial P}{\partial y} =2+ 3 = 5 . Hence, Green's Theorem implies

p.m: \begin{array}{lcl} \int_{C} \vec{F} \cdot d\vec{r}\amp = \amp \iint_D \left( \frac{\partial Q}{\partial x} - \frac{\partial P}{\partial y} \right) dA \\ \amp =\amp \iint_D 5 dA \\ \amp = \amp 5 \int_0^{\pi/3} \int_0^{3} r \, dr \, d\theta \quad \text{[Using polar coordinates]} \\\amp = \amp 5 \left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right) \left(\frac{ 3^2}{2}\right) \\\amp =\amp {\frac{15}{2}} \pi \end{array}
